title: Unmatched Adventures: Tales to Amaze! - Review
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oRXt4EmUmKk

In the Dungeon Dive's last video of 2023, Daniel (@dungeondive) finally tries the Unmatched system through its co-op spin-off, Unmatched Adventures: Tales to Amaze. He rarely plays two-player games, so a cooperative version appealed. It has a B-movie cast of heroes: the Golden Bat, Dr. Jill Trent with her sidekick Daisy, Annie Christmas with Charlie, and Nikola Tesla. They face the Mothman, who hates bridges, or the Martian Invaders, along with cryptid minions like the Skunk Ape, the Blob, a giant tarantula, an ant queen, the Jersey Devil and the Loveland Frog.

He praises the product: a superb insert, pre-washed minis and a smooth journey from box to table. The colour-coded circle map (he suspects inspiration from Tannhäuser) handles zones and line of sight elegantly. Each fighter's deck is both their abilities and their life, because running out of cards is deadly, so knowing when to push or hold back is the core decision. Villains act from their own decks via a shuffled initiative deck. The Blob leaves acid tokens, the spider lays webs, the Mothman's threat track destroys bridges, and optional event cards turn up the difficulty.

His verdict is that it's fun, light and King of Tokyo-like, better with friends than solo, and excellent value next to the pricey, incomplete Dice Throne Adventures. But it doesn't feel like an adventure at all: there's no journey, no growth, no unfolding narrative. A good game with a misleading title.

----

What does a game need before it earns the word "Adventure" in its title? Does Unmatched Adventures qualify for you?
